newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Argentina, Vietnam sign science, agriculture pacts.
newsitem.headline: Argentina, Vietnam sign science, agriculture pacts.

text.p: Argentina and Vietnam signed accords on agricultural and science cooperation on Monday as President Carlos Menem began the first visit by a South American head of state to the communist country.

Menem, on a three-stop tour of Southeast Asia, arrived in Hanoi overnight and was formally greeted on Monday with an honour guard at the presidential palace, where women in traditional silk dresses threw flowers at his feet.

He oversaw signing of the accords with Vietnam's Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet. Details of the pacts were not available, but afterwards Kiet told journalists the event reflected a strengthening relationship between the two nations.
Menem, who was accompanied by large diplomatic and business delegations, was due to attend a series of commerce seminars later in the day and attend the opening of an embassy in Hanoi on Tuesday.

Diplomats said his Southeast Asia tour, beginning in Vietnam and continuing to Thailand and Singapore, is aimed at building ties between Argentina and a region containing some of the world's most dynamic economies.
Two-way trade with Vietnam is meagre -- little more than $10 million a year -- and mostly in Argentina's favour.
Vietnam President Le Duc Anh, who would normally officiate at ceremonies welcoming a visiting head of state, was recovering from a stroke suffered last November and did not attend Monday's events.
Vietnam's links with Latin America have grown in recent years. Hanoi has long-standing ties with fellow communist state Cuba and President Anh visited Brazil in 1995.
